celaleyn:1-1.t: Meccan; seven ayahs counting the basmala, if it is part of it, in which case the seventh is ﴿صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ﴾; and if it is not part of it, then the seventh is ﴿غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ﴾. At its beginning "قُولُوا" ("Say") is implied (muqaddar), so that what precedes "إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ" fits with it, by its being part of what the servants say. ﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ a declarative (khabariyya) sentence whose intent is to praise Allah by its content, namely that He, Exalted is He, owns all praise from creation, or that He deserves that they praise Him. "Allah" is a proper name for the One truly worshipped. ﴿رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ i.e. the Owner of all creation: humans, jinn, angels, beasts and others. Each of these is called an ʿālam ("world"): one says "the world of humans", "the world of jinn", and so on. In its plural with yāʾ and nūn, those endowed with reason are given precedence over the others. It is derived from ʿalāma ("sign"), because it is a sign of the One who brought it into being.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ i.e. the Possessor of mercy, which is willing good for those worthy of it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ i.e. of the Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. It is mentioned specifically because on that day no one has any manifest dominion except Allah the Exalted, as evidenced by {لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ لِلَّهِ}. Whoever reads {مَالِكِ}, its meaning is: the Owner of the whole affair on the Day of Resurrection, i.e. He is described by that permanently, {كَغَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ} (like "Forgiver of sin"); hence it is valid for it to occur as a ṣifa (adjective) of a definite noun.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾ i.e. we single You out for worship, including tawḥīd (affirming Your oneness) and other things, and we seek help in worship and in other things.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ i.e. guide us to it. From it is made a badal (substitute):

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ with guidance. And from الَّذِينَ, together with its ṣila (relative clause), is made a badal: ﴿غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ and they are the Jews; ﴿وَلَا﴾ i.e. and not ﴿الضَّالِّينَ﴾ and they are the Christians. The subtle point (nukta) of the badal is to convey that the rightly guided are neither Jews nor Christians.
